source-integrity.tradability: validated by current Workgraph identity record
source-integrity.provenance: Current issuer Q2 2026 results and SEC 2026 proxy supplement cumulative Scout/Beta evidence; issuer duplicates are not counted as independent origins.
source-integrity.freshness: Q2 2026 results dated 2026-07-22 and 2026 proxy dated 2026-03-04.
source-integrity.sourceIndependence: SEC governance disclosure is distinct from issuer earnings release; no unsupported independent market claim is used to raise scores.

company-underwriting.thesis: TI is showing a broad cyclical recovery with materially stronger cash generation while its 300mm manufacturing strategy provides cost and supply leverage across analog and embedded markets; large fixed-capacity investment and semiconductor cyclicality remain central risks.
company-underwriting.keyRisk: If industrial/automotive/data-center demand weakens, new capacity can become an underutilized fixed-cost burden and compress returns despite the current cash-flow rebound.
company-underwriting.nextCatalyst: Q3 2026 revenue/EPS delivery against the stated $5.65-$6.15B revenue and $2.23-$2.57 EPS outlook, plus evidence on utilization and returns from 300mm capacity.

thesisQuality.basis: Q2 revenue rose 23% year over year with broad industrial, data-center and automotive growth; 300mm production supports a differentiated cost/supply thesis, though cyclicality limits durability certainty.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Q2 revenue +23%, operating profit +48%, net income +53%; trailing-12-month operating cash flow was $8.7B and free cash flow $6.5B, up sharply year over year.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: Operating recovery is strong, but the cited primary sources do not establish compelling current-price valuation headroom; score remains mixed rather than assuming favorable asymmetry.

catalystScore.basis: Q3 guidance calls for $5.65-$6.15B revenue and $2.23-$2.57 EPS, providing a clear near-term execution checkpoint; catalyst set is credible but primarily cyclical/operational.

governancePower.basis: Current SEC proxy documents board/accountability structure while TI returned $5.8B to owners over 12 months and continued R&D/capacity investment, supporting disciplined long-duration capital allocation with cyclical execution risk.

alignment2036.basis: Analog and embedded semiconductors enable sensing, power and control across industrial, automotive and data-center systems, linking TI to durable electrification/automation infrastructure needs.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Broad growth across industrial, data center and automotive plus analog and embedded segments demonstrates multiple demand engines reusing manufacturing and product capabilities.

bottleneckControl.basis: Large internally controlled 300mm capacity creates cost and supply leverage and long lead-time manufacturing capability, but customers retain alternative semiconductor suppliers.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Diversified end markets and strong cash generation support resilience, while semiconductor cyclicality and fixed-capacity utilization remain material scenario dependencies.

substitutionResilience.basis: Large analog/embedded portfolio and manufacturing scale create qualification and cost barriers, though individual semiconductor functions remain competitively substitutable.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Issuer explicitly attributes business-model benefits to 300mm production and has substantial internal manufacturing investment, supporting supply control; geopolitical and utilization risks prevent an exceptional score.

pricingPower.basis: Operating profit grew faster than revenue during broad recovery and analog operating profit rose 50%, supporting improving economics, but evidence does not isolate durable price pass-through from utilization/mix.

riskEvidence.basis: Primary risks are semiconductor cyclicality, fixed-cost underutilization and returns on large manufacturing investment; strong current free cash flow and broad demand recovery reduce near-term financial stress.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Current primary operating/cash-flow evidence and SEC governance evidence are strong, with validated identity and existing causal evidence; confidence is reduced by limited current valuation and utilization detail.
